prompt_text: Who is a reliable contractor in Joplin MO for a home remodel or repair project?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t run a live search, so I can’t point to a currently vetted company name from Joplin for you — but I can help you find a reliable local contractor and vet any candidates you find. A few quick questions that will help me give targeted names if you want to look them up yourself: what kind of job is it (kitchen/bath remodel, roofing, foundation, plumbing, general remodel, etc.), what’s your budget, and when do you need it done?

How to find a reliable contractor in Joplin
- Start local: check the Joplin Area Chamber of Commerce member directory and local Facebook community groups (people often post recent recommendations).  
- Use reputable aggregator/review sites: Better Business Bureau (BBB), Angi/HomeAdvisor, Houzz, and Yelp — look for companies with many recent 4–5 star reviews and written responses to complaints.  
- Ask friends/neighbors or post in local community groups for referrals; seeing completed work in person is very helpful.  
- Get at least three written bids so you can compare scope, materials, and price.

How to vet candidates
- Licensing/registration: confirm the contractor is registered with the appropriate Missouri or local authority for the trade (electrical/plumbing often require licensed tradespeople). Contact the City of Joplin Building/Permits office to confirm permit requirements and whether the contractor pulls permits.  
- Insurance: get a certificate of liability insurance and proof of workers’ compensation (or a signed waiver if they use no employees). Call the insurer to confirm coverage is active.  
- References: ask for 3 recent job references (similar scope) and follow up. Ask to see photos or visit a completed job nearby if possible.  
- Written contract: require a detailed contract showing scope, schedule, payment schedule (avoid large up-front cash payments), materials, warranty, cleanup, and dispute resolution.  
- Timeline and communication: make sure they give a realistic timeline and announce a primary contact.

Questions to ask a contractor
- Are you licensed/registered for this trade in Missouri/Joplin? Can you provide license/registration numbers?  
- Can you provide proof of liability insurance and workers’ comp? (Get the insurer name and call to verify.)  
- Will you pull the required permits and arrange inspections?  
- Who will supervise day-to-day work and who will be on-site?  
- Can you give three recent references from similar projects?  
- What is the projected start and completion date? What’s the payment schedule?  
- What warranties do you offer on labor and materials?

Red flags
- No written contract or insists on large upfront cash payment.  
- Unwilling to provide references or proof of insurance.  
- Extremely low bid compared to others with vague scope.  
- Poor communication, no timeline, or refuses to pull permits.

Next steps I can help with
- If you share 2–3 contractor names (or links to their profiles/ads), I can help you evaluate reviews, wording in their quotes, and list specific questions to ask them.  
- I can provide a sample contract checklist or a short message you can send to contractors requesting estimates and documents.

Tell me the project type and any names you already have and I’ll help you vet them.
